# Fabiola Campuzano

I'm a recent UCLA graduate with degrees in Statistics & Data Science and Cognitive Science with a Specialization in Computing, with experience in behavioral research, experimental design, and data analysis. 

## About Me

I'm interested in understanding human behavior and health through research. 

I'm passionate about topics related to neuroscience, psychology, mental health, and public health, and using applied statistics and machine learning.

Outside of research and data, I like to go to concerts, read, watch movies, and listen to music. My top three favorite movies are The Truman Show, Donnie Darko, and Whiplash!  

## Current Work

I currently work as a research assistant in the Rissman Memory Lab at UCLA, supporting a cognitive neuroscience study examining memory, consolidation, and cognition using behavioral, physiological, and EEG methods.

My work includes developing and programming experiential methods into 4 Qualtrics surveys, including cognitive measures, questionnaires, and post-encoding memory assessments. I also contributed to study development by conducting a literature review, evaluating experimental stimuli, developing memory-test questions, and refining participant procedures.

I also aim to write accessible, research-informed articles exploring psychology, neuroscience, mental health, and related topics. My goal is to translate scientific research into digestible and engaging explanations for a general audience.
